column1: # The server-response table: one HTTP request per row, replayed against the
# port by tests/server_responses.rs and against the pinned Haskell server by
# tests/capture_haskell_fixtures.sh, which writes the captures under
# haskell-responses/.  Add a row, re-run the capture, commit both.
#   Start one fresh server with <theory> as theory index 1 (a bare name is a
#   file of tests/fixtures/, anything else is workspace-relative).  The rows
#   below it run against that server in file order, on both sides, so a
#   stateful sequence replays identically.  Config tokens tweak only the
#   port's harness: `maude=missing` points every proof session started after
#   the load at a missing Maude.
#   method   GET, POST, or UPLOAD:<file> (POST / with the file as the
#            The port's answer, which the capture also checks against the
#            oracle's (except for `diverge` rows; a `redirect` row only needs
#            a 3xx from the oracle).  `-` leaves the content type unchecked.
#   compare  bytes       the body, byte for byte
#            load-stamp  the same, with the theory's load time and origin path
#                        blanked (a capture run cannot share them)
#            banner      the same, with the build values of the `Generated
#                        from:` banner blanked (the port prints them empty)
#            contains:<a>\n<b>  each line occurs in both bodies (where the
#                        port's wording or framing differs by design)
#            redirect    the Location header (the capture holds the oracle's)
#            diverge     a documented divergence: the body must differ from
#            diverge:<c> a documented divergence: the oracle answers something
#                        else (checked at capture time), the port answers the
#   capture  The file under haskell-responses/; `-` for none.  Several rows
#            may name one capture: the capture script checks that the oracle
#            answers each of them with the same bytes.
# The read-only routes on one theory.

column1: # `PathPiece Int` reads a leading zero and a plus sign, and Yesod dispatches on
# percent-decoded segments: all of these are theory 1.
# `next`/`prev` walk the theory paths for the `normal` section only.
# `verify/lemma` falls through to the help view.
# Past the end of the ranked methods (two at the `debug` root) is the
# "Sorry" alert.  A non-positive index passes upstream's `length methods >= i`
# guard and raises in `!!` (minBound wraps to maxBound), an alert quoting the
# GHC CallStack; the port answers the one "Sorry" alert for all of them.
# Yesod's Not Found page echoes the raw request path (percent-encoding kept,
# query dropped), whatever raised it: an unknown index, an index piece
# `PathPiece Int` cannot read, a theory path `parseTheoryPath` rejects, or no
# route at all.  Never a path-extractor 400.  /static is a separate WAI app
# `PathPiece Bool` reads only `True`/`False`, the bound is an `Int`, and
# The graph routes.  `/intdot` is a shell whatever the path, its `dotsrc` the
# same path on the json route; the dot routes draw source cases and proof
# nodes, and every other theory path is their catch-all `error`, a 500.  The
# json route answers an unresolvable proof path with an empty 200, the dot
# An invalid source or case index reaches one of the two unchecked `!!`s of
# `cases !! (i-1) !! (j-1)`: the source lookup fails first, whatever the case
# index, and minBound wraps to maxBound when one is subtracted.
# The port does not serve diff theories (they need `ClosedDiffTheory`): it
# answers an alert where the oracle answers its Not Found page.
# The rows that replace theory 1 in place come last: `verify/proof` rebuilds
# No lemma is marked modified, so nothing is appended to the file.
# Navigation reads only the loaded theory: it answers without the prover.
# Autoprove and a method application each allocate the next index, on both
# sides.  Autoproving the proved snapshot still answers a fresh index; a
# negative bound means unbounded.  The searched node keeps its system (the
# web session's SysRetention::KeepAll), so its graph is not empty.
# Deleting a lemma or a proof step publishes the edited theory at the next
# An explicitly removed proof step still renders as removed after deleting
# the reusable lemma that precedes it.
# A [sources] lemma is deleted like any other.
# An unguarded source lemma blocks publication while it survives. Removing
# the lemma also removes its assumption, so the port can publish the edit.
# Uploads (`POST /`): a theory is installed at the next index; an empty file
# and a parse failure are banners over the index.  The port's parse
# diagnostic differs from Parsec's by design.  Unloading redirects to the
# index, which then lists only the upload.
# `abbrevInBackend` abbreviates every premise and conclusion term of size >= 30.
# A failing oracle (`heuristic=o`, no ./oracle next to the theory) is an alert
# for the request that ranked, and publishes nothing.  The oracle's alert is
# the exception `evalInThread` caught; the port answers the prover-failure
# alert instead (its ranking failure is typed, not an exception).
# A terminal proof node renders without resolving the unused, missing tactic.
# `makeWfErrorsHtml` puts the wellformedness report into the banner unescaped.
# The overview counts the rules of the deduplicated protocol cache.
# A source case name too long for the ribbon wraps at the HTML line width.
